subject: GCP Private Offer — early adopter SKU tiers & reseller split
messages:
From: Peter Huang <peter@healthscale.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: partner@distribucloud.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a GCP private offer — packaging and reseller split

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re interested in moving to a GCP private offer to cover our inference usage for MH models. A couple of asks from procurement: 

- We want an early-adopter tier (first 12 months) with a 15% list discount on reserved capacity SKUs.
- Our reseller, DistribuCloud, will handle billing — they asked what reseller pass-through percentage Redwood can commit to.
- We also need guidance on SKU bundling: do you recommend a single reserved SKU + metered token add-on, or two SKUs (reserved + embeddings) to simplify billing?

I attached our mutual-action plan (MAAP) draft. Can you outline a recommended structure and confirm whether the 15% early-adopter discount is feasible with a 10–12% reseller split?

Regards,
Peter
Director of Cloud Procurement
HealthScale Inc

Attachments: HealthScale_MAAP_v1.xlsx
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Peter Huang <peter@healthscale.com>
Cc: partner@distribucloud.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a GCP private offer — packaging and reseller split

Hi Peter — great to hear HealthScale is ready to progress. Quick answers up front, then detail below.

- Early-adopter 15% off list: we can accommodate this off a 12‑month reserved commitment if committed volumes hit the MAAP thresholds.
- Reseller pass-through: a 10% reseller split is workable; 12% is near the upper bound but can be approved on a one-time onboarding uplift (we'd convert that into a fixed channel credit).
- SKU packaging: recommend two SKUs — a reserved capacity SKU (node-hour or slot) and a metered token SKU for variable inference. That keeps usage reporting clean and avoids re-architecting billing when you vary embeddings vs. generation.

Attached is a draft private-offer term sheet (PDF) and a short sketch of the pricing waterfall that maps list price -> early-adopter discount -> reseller credit -> net to Redwood. Highlights below: 

1) Reserved SKU: list price set to target unit economics; early-adopter 15% off list applied at invoice time for first 12 months.
2) Metered SKU: standard list with a 10% volume discount at pre-agreed thresholds (same 12-month window).
3) Reseller handling: DistribuCloud invoices HealthScale. Redwood issues a partner credit (10% of list) to DistribuCloud monthly; we can make that 12% for the first 3 months to cover onboarding if HealthScale agrees to a longer commit term (18 months).

Next steps: Ben and Laura (cc’d) will validate the margin math and confirm whether we can formalize the 12% temporary uplift and the proposed fallback guardrails. If that’s approved, I’ll issue a GCP private-offer draft and we can start the marketplace flow.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: GCP_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a GCP private offer — packaging and reseller split

Tessa — quick margin check (notes for the thread):

- If list price for reserved SKU = $3.20/node-hour, 15% early-adopter = $2.72 effective. With infra & ops unit cost ~ $1.10, gross contribution still looks fine at scale.
- 10% reseller credit at list reduces Redwood net further: 3.20 * 0.90 = 2.88 before early-adopter; we need to apply order of operations consistently. Proposal: compute partner credit as percentage of list (not post-discount) to keep distributor economics stable.
- Approve temporary 12% onboarding uplift for first 90 days, converted to a fixed credit amortized over first invoice period. Require a fallback: if actual consumption drops below 70% of committed volume in months 4–6, revert to standard 10% and pro-rate the uplift back.

I'll prepare the exact numbers and add to the term sheet PDF; Laura please confirm compliance and revenue recognition flags.

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Commercial Ops
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a GCP private offer — packaging and reseller split

Ben — flagged items from RevOps / Legal: 

- Partner credit basis: agree with list-based calculation (credit = pct of list price) to avoid messy recalcs in the marketplace invoice. Document that explicitly.
- Accounting: the temporary 12% uplift must be disclosed as a one-time onboarding credit in the contract; we should not shift revenue recognition rules. We’ll need a short clause that allows us to claw back the uplift pro-rata if commit is not met in months 4–6.
- SKU design: two SKUs is cleaner for invoicing and for future audits. Make sure the reserved SKU has a clear definition (node type, effective concurrency, and included KV cache units).

I’ll add a short contract snippet and return a redline by end of day. Once we have DistribuCloud’s confirmation on pass-through mechanics, we can proceed to docu-sign and GCP marketplace initiation.

-LB
From: DistribuCloud Partner <partner@distribucloud.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Peter Huang <peter@healthscale.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a GCP private offer — packaging and reseller split

Hi all — DistribuCloud here. We can accept a 12% partner pass-through on the reserved SKU for the first 90 days as an onboarding uplift. Two minor asks: 

1) Minimum list price floor: we require the reserved SKU list price not be lower than $2.75/node-hour to protect our margin on billing fees.
2) Evidence for consumption: we need a monthly CSV report (tokens & node-hours) to reconcile actuals before any uplift clawback. Could Redwood supply that via a secure Drive link or SFTP?

If those two items are in the term sheet we’re ready to proceed. Peter — happy to coordinate the PO issuance once Redwood finalizes the doc.

Best,
Aarti Mehra
Channel Ops, DistribuCloud
